# `@elabs/components-tokens`

> Semantic CSS-variable themes + ThemeProvider/useTheme.

Part of **brand-ui**, a source-owned, token-driven React component system.
These packages are **private** and are not published to any registry — they are
consumed from this workspace. See `docs/CONSUMING.md`.

## Install

Inside this monorepo the packages resolve as workspace dependencies:

```json
"@elabs/components-tokens": "workspace:*"
```

## Set up styling (do not skip)

Components are Tailwind v4 classes backed by semantic tokens. Two lines in
your CSS entry, or **everything renders unstyled** — the single most common
mistake:

```css
@import "@elabs/components-tokens/styles.css";
@source "../node_modules/@elabs/components-tokens/dist";
```

The `@source` line is required because Tailwind ignores `node_modules`. Add
one per brand-ui package you render. Then wrap your app once:

```tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from "@elabs/components-tokens";

<ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">{children}</ThemeProvider>;
```

## This package specifically

- `tailwindcss` `^4` is a peer — it must be the SAME instance that processes the token stylesheet.
- Ships the shipped themes and the self-hosted fonts. Everything else depends on this package.
- Font smoothing is already applied: the stylesheet's `@layer base` `body` rule sets `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased` and `-moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale`. **Do not re-add those two lines in your app CSS** — importing `styles.css` is enough. It is a base-layer rule, so an app that genuinely wants subpixel rendering can still override it.

## What's in it

19 exported components — including `BUILT_IN_THEME_DEFINITIONS`, `BUILT_IN_THEME_META`, `BUILT_IN_THEMES`, `DECORATION_LEVELS`, `DecorationProvider`.

Don't guess the API — ask the CLI:

```bash
pnpm add -D @elabs/components-cli
pnpm exec brand-ui search <query>   # find a component
pnpm exec brand-ui docs <Name>      # its real props, from source
```

## Using an AI coding agent?

For Claude Code, install the plugin from this repo's checkout:

```
/plugin marketplace add .
/plugin install brand-ui
```

`brand-ui docs <Name>` returns intent, composition, state→token mappings and
anti-patterns — tell your agent to run it instead of guessing a prop. The CLI
also runs as an MCP server (`brand-ui mcp`).

## The focus ring (`--ring`)

`--ring` is the **focus indicator**: a graphical mark, brand-derived, distinct
from every role it can co-occur with. The contract
(`docs/ADR/0027-focus-ring-token-contract.md`,
issue #427) — a theme's `--ring` must satisfy all of:

1. **Brand family** — within ~20° of that theme's `--primary` hue, at a
   clearly different lightness/chroma rung (never an alias).
2. **1.4.11 (≥3:1)** against `--background`, `--card`, `--surface-muted`,
   `--muted` and `--secondary` — a focus ring lands on all five.
3. **Distinctness (ΔE ≥ 0.05 OKLab)** from `--primary`, `--chart-1`,
   `--accent-foreground` (`MUST_DIFFER`), `--info` (`ROLE_PAIRS`) and
   `--success` (new row, Part C).
4. **`--sidebar-ring: var(--ring)`** is the sanctioned mirror — an override
   reaches sidebar focus automatically. Never re-declare it with a literal.
5. **Overriding it is supported**, in a `[data-theme="…"]`-scoped block,
   provided (1)–(3) still hold. Verify with `pnpm roles:check` and
   `pnpm --filter @elabs/components-tokens test`. **Prefer
   forking the theme (`/new-theme`) over patching one token.**
6. `:root`'s blue ring is **not** an exception — `:root`'s `--primary` is a
   blue (264°) and its ring is the same hue at a distinct rung (ΔE 0.1044). It
   already satisfies this contract.

### Overriding `--ring`

An override is a supported path, not a private fork — but it is scoped to the
theme it changes and it has to keep satisfying constraints (1)–(3) above.

```css
/* Your app's CSS, after importing @elabs/components-tokens/styles.css */
[data-theme="light"] {
  --ring: oklch(0.4 0.13 140);
}
```

Before you ship it, check the same three constraints the contract states:

- **Brand family** — within ~20° of your theme's `--primary` hue, at a
  clearly different lightness/chroma rung.
- **1.4.11 (≥3:1)** against `--background`, `--card`, `--surface-muted`,
  `--muted` and `--secondary`.
- **Distinctness (ΔE ≥ 0.05 OKLab)** from `--primary`, `--chart-1`,
  `--accent-foreground`, `--info` and `--success`.

Then verify against the repo's own gates:

```bash
pnpm roles:check
pnpm --filter @elabs/components-tokens test
```

`--sidebar-ring: var(--ring)` mirrors your override into the sidebar
automatically — nothing else to change there.

**Prefer forking the theme with `/new-theme`
over patching one token.** A single-token override doesn't get the review a
shipped theme gets, and it is easy to satisfy the letter of the three
constraints while missing something a full theme pass would catch. Reach for
the override recipe above only for a small, well-understood nudge.
